key: And ye shall take you on the first day the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm-trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and ye shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
s: Closing the calendar of feasts, the law of tabernacles follows the harvest; the Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 30:12, reads the four kinds as Israel’s people, with both Torah and good deeds, with one, or with neither, bound in one bundle to atone for one another.

evidence.words: פְּרִי עֵץ הָדָר, אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מָה אֶתְרוֹג זֶה יֵשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ רֵיחַ, כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם תּוֹרָה וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים … וְעַרְבֵי נָחַל, אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מָה עֲרָבָה זוֹ אֵין בָּהּ טַעַם וְאֵין בָּהּ רֵיחַ, כָּךְ הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לֹא תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים … אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יֻקְשְׁרוּ כֻלָּם אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת וְהֵן מְכַפְּרִין אֵלּוּ עַל אֵלּוּ
evidence.gloss: The fruit of a goodly tree: this is Israel; as the citron has taste and has fragrance, so Israel has people who have Torah and have good deeds … Willows of the brook: this is Israel; as the willow has no taste and no fragrance, so Israel has people who have neither Torah nor good deeds … The Holy One, blessed be He, said: let them all be bound in one bundle, and they will atone for one another.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Leviticus 23:40, at [112,40] match). Plain sense faithful: 23:39 to 43 close the chapter’s calendar with the feast kept when the fruits of the land are gathered in. Leviticus Rabbah 30:12, printed on 23:40 in the packet, reads citron, palm, myrtle and willow each as Israel: people with Torah and good deeds, with Torah only, with good deeds only, with neither; God says let them all be bound in one bundle and they will atone for one another. The sentence carries exactly that, without drift; read the whole run of 30:1 to 30:16 on the verse (30:9 to 30:11 give other allegories, God, the patriarchs, the Sanhedrin), and 30:12 is correctly named. entry-check ok, 44 words.
